liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playin' In The Band** (2 reviews): The first-set closer is long and good; the band could still dig into it after the layoff; Reviewer hears a long Playin' that charges into the final verse with a bang [10][13]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 review): Keith's playing stands out in the intro, which is a jazzy version; the preceding Wheel is mellow with a hot jam before the close [13]
- **Dancin' in the Streets** (1 review): Crazy Fingers leads into a huge Dancin', possibly one of the best versions [17]
- **Cosmic Charlie** (1 review): Cosmic Charlie is singled out as especially sweet [19]
- **Slipknot!** (1 review): Slipknot is described as mindbending, within a strong second set that also has a very nice High Time [10]

## The recordings

- **gd76-06-14.sbd.hollister.22804.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 201 min; rated 4.61/5 by 74 [1]. Said about its sound: Betty Cantor's board recording from June '76 is at her best; sound quality is rated top-notch; Crisp sound with no noticeable problems; Keith is easy to pick out in the mix; Recording is exceptionally beautiful, with wide instrumental range; Donna's backing vocals are clearly in tune on Crazy Fingers [10][13][18]
- **gd1976-06-14.sbd.bettycantor.gems.82308.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 201 min; rated 4.83/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd1976-06-14.143026.sbd.betty.composite.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: soundboard; 25 songs; 204 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1976-06-14.sbd.hollister.13966.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 201 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [4]

## Around the show

- Recommends also hearing the 15 June show for a blistering Let It Grow [16]
- Reviewer judges it the best-sounding show of 1976 [19]
- Early 1976 shows sound rusty after the year off from touring, but by mid-June the band had found its groove again [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-06-14.sbd.hollister.22804.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer's earlier copy was a hissy Maxell XL II tape from a radio broadcast, dating from 1982; Soundboard source from the Hollister lineage; Lazy Lightning runs into Supplication and Crazy Fingers flows through to Franklin's Tower [1][17]
- **gd1976-06-14.sbd.bettycantor.gems.82308.flac16**: taped by SBD DAT from the collection of Todd Evans; transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Betty Board > PCM > DAT [2]. Also: Betty Cantor soundboard recording, a GEMS production; long tunings and dead air were given their own tracks [2]
- **gd1976-06-14.143026.sbd.betty.composite.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Betty Cantor and Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Primary Source: Betty's 7" two track Master Soundboard Reels @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM > Dat (16-bit/44.1k); Secondary Source: Betty's 7" two track Master… [3]
- **gd1976-06-14.sbd.hollister.13966.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Hollister; source: S:MR>PCM>DAT>CD>EAC>SHN [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Crimson Records: [GRATEFUL DEAD – Beacon Theatre ’76 - Crimson Records](https://crimsonrecords.com.ar/product/grateful-dead-beacon-theatre-76/) [22]
- Poster by Peter Bickmore: [Grateful Dead Live at Beacon Theatre on 1976-06-14](https://edeadshop.com/blogs/crew-tunes/grateful-dead-live-at-beacon-theatre-on-1976-06-14) [23]
- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1976-06-14 Beacon Theatre, New York, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1976-06-14-beacon-theatre-new-york-ny-usa/) [24]
- Poster by Snooky Flowers Grateful Dead: [1976-06-15 Beacon Theatre, New York, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1976-06-15-beacon-theatre-new-york-ny-usa/) [25]
